Braak 0: Cells from an aged human brain with no neurofibrillary tangle pathology: neuronal tau homeostasis is intact, with no detectable neurofibrillary degeneration in any region.
Braak II: Cells from a human brain with very early neurofibrillary pathology: tau-bearing neurofibrillary tangles largely confined to the transentorhinal and entorhinal cortex, with preserved neocortical integrity.
Braak III: Cells from a human brain with limbic-stage neurofibrillary pathology: tangles extend through the hippocampus and limbic structures, with early involvement of association cortex and emerging synaptic stress.
Braak IV: Cells from a human brain with advancing limbic neurofibrillary pathology: dense tangle burden in hippocampus and entorhinal cortex, spreading into temporal isocortex, accompanied by reactive glia and synaptic dysfunction.
Braak V: Cells from a human brain with isocortical neurofibrillary pathology: widespread tangle involvement of neocortical association areas, substantial neuronal loss, gliosis and impaired cortical connectivity.
Braak VI: Cells from a human brain with severe end-stage neurofibrillary pathology: devastating tangle burden across virtually all cortical areas including primary sensory regions, marked neuronal loss and gliosis.
nan: Cells from a human brain with uncharacterized neuropathology.
